questions.q: In this lab's scenario, why is "Customer Order Processing" chosen as the Business Service?
options: Because it is the name of one specific database CI
Because it is a name a non-technical stakeholder, like a VP of Sales, would recognize and care about directly, defined by the outcome it provides
Because it is the first CI created in Chapter 1
Because Business Services must always be named after departments
questions.explain: The Business Service is chosen by business recognition and outcome, not by technical detail.

questions.q: What does the "Order Processing Application" Technical Service represent in this lab?
options: A second, unrelated Business Service
A report summarizing Incident counts
The three-tier application stack itself, built from the exact CIs modeled in Chapters 1 and 2
A location record for the data center hosting the servers
questions.explain: The Technical Service is the bridge between the business-facing name and the real web/application/database server CIs underneath it.

questions.q: What happens if the database server CI exists but was never connected to the Technical Service record?
options: Nothing changes — the chain still works correctly
The chain breaks at that exact point, and impact analysis from the Business Service level would silently miss that CI
The CI is automatically deleted
The Business Service record is automatically renamed
questions.explain: A missing link anywhere in the Business Service to Technical Service to CI chain causes impact analysis to silently miss the disconnected CI.

questions.q: Once the chain is confirmed, how should the database server failing be described at the Business Service level?
options: "Customer Order Processing is down -- customers cannot place or complete orders"
"The order database server is down" (the CI-level description)
"The Order Processing Application is degraded" (the Technical Service-level description)
No description is possible at the Business Service level
questions.explain: Each altitude gets its own accurate description of the same fact; the Business Service-level answer is framed in terms the business recognizes.

questions.q: According to the lab's final check, what makes a CSDM model actually finished?
options: Having at least one CI somewhere in the CMDB, regardless of connections
Naming the Business Service the way the business recognizes it, building the Technical Service from real CIs, and tracing every CI upward with no missing links
Having the Technical Service record exist, even if left as an empty placeholder
Running impact analysis once, regardless of the result
questions.explain: Missing any one of those three conditions means the model isn't actually finished, even if some CIs and relationships exist in the CMDB.
